skill.name: flow-finishing-branch
skill.description: Guide developers through Git branch completion choices, including pull requests, squash merges, fast-forward merges, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Choose a safe Git branch completion path based on review, history, and cleanup needs.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: The external-command alerts are Markdown code fence false positives, not Ruby backtick execution. The path traversal alerts are documentation links, not filesystem access. A prompt-like `[PROTOCOL]` footer directs the agent to check `CLAUDE.md`, which creates a real prompt-injection risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the `[PROTOCOL]` footer or rewrite it as an author note. Do not direct the agent to read other repo instructions.
Add confirmation guidance before branch deletion. Tell users to preserve needed work before local or remote cleanup.
Mark Git and GitHub CLI commands as examples. Require users to adapt branch names and follow repository policy.

content.value_statement: Finishing a branch requires choosing between fast merge, pull request, squash, or cleanup. This skill provides a structured decision path for safer Git completion work.
actual_capabilities: Compares fast-forward merge, pull request, squash merge, and cleanup choices.
Uses file count, review need, and history quality to select an action.
Lists readiness checks for tests, builds, lint, documentation, logs, and clean worktree.
Provides example Git and GitHub CLI commands for each branch outcome.
Encourages pull requests for team projects and production code.
limitations: Does not run Git commands or verify repository state automatically.
Uses placeholder branch names, so users must adapt commands.
Does not evaluate protected branch rules or CI provider settings.
Cleanup guidance can delete branches if users skip confirmation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Team Pull Request
use_cases.description: Choose a review-first path for production code with CI checks and an audit trail.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Abandoned Work
use_cases.description: Decide when failed experiments should be preserved, deleted locally, or removed from remote branches.

use_cases.title: Select a Release Merge Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare fast-forward, squash, and pull request paths before completing a release branch.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Finish Option
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-finishing-branch to choose how I should finish my current branch. Ask for missing context before recommending an option.

prompt_templates.title: Check Merge Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-finishing-branch to review my branch readiness. Check tests, build, lint, docs, logs, and uncommitted changes before merge advice.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-finishing-branch for an abandoned branch. Help me decide what to preserve, what to delete, and what warnings to show.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Team Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-finishing-branch to draft a branch completion policy for a team repository with protected main, CI gates, and required reviews.

output_examples.input: Small private branch, three changed files, clean commits, no review required.
output_examples.output: Recommended action: fast-forward merge. Verify tests and build first. Delete the local branch only after the merge succeeds.

output_examples.input: Production change with required review, CI checks, and messy work-in-progress commits.
output_examples.output: Recommended action: create a pull request. Use review and CI as the completion gate. Squash only if the commit history is noisy.

output_examples.input: Failed experiment branch with no useful changes and a remote branch already pushed.
output_examples.output: Recommended action: cleanup only. Confirm the work is no longer needed. Preserve useful patches before deleting local or remote branches.

best_practices: Run tests, build, and lint before selecting any completion path.
Use a pull request when review, CI, or audit records matter.
Confirm branch deletion with the team before cleanup.
anti_patterns: Deleting a branch before preserving useful work.
Skipping CI because the change looks small.
Squashing commits when detailed history is needed for debugging.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example commands that users must review before use.

faq.question: When should I create a pull request?
faq.answer: Use a pull request for team projects, production code, review records, or CI verification.

faq.question: Can I use it with protected branches?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must follow the repository rules and branch protection settings.

faq.question: Does it support squash merges?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends squash merges when many small commits should become one logical change.

faq.question: What should I do before cleanup?
faq.answer: Confirm the work is abandoned and preserve any useful patches before deleting branches.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
